events.text: Utterson stays behind after Jekyll's dinner to speak with him.
events.quote: Mr. Utterson so contrived that he remained behind after the others had departed

events.text: Utterson raises the subject of Jekyll's will.
events.quote: I have been wanting to speak to you, Jekyll

events.text: Jekyll calls Lanyon a hide-bound pedant and says he was disappointed in him.
events.quote: I was never more disappointed in any man than Lanyon

events.text: Utterson says he has learned something of young Hyde.
events.quote: I have been learning something of young Hyde

events.text: Jekyll pales and refuses to hear more about Hyde.
events.quote: I do not care to hear more

events.text: Utterson offers to help Jekyll out of the matter in confidence.
events.quote: Make a clean breast of this in confidence

events.text: Jekyll says he can be rid of Mr. Hyde whenever he chooses.
events.quote: the moment I choose, I can be rid of Mr. Hyde

events.text: Jekyll says he takes a great interest in poor Hyde.
events.quote: I have really a very great interest in poor Hyde

events.text: Jekyll asks Utterson to help Hyde for his sake when he is gone.
events.quote: I only ask you to help him for my sake

events.text: Utterson promises to bear with Hyde and get his rights for him.
